summary.text: Ryan Peterman, a Democrat and former Navy officer, lost the November 3, 2026 election for Iowa Secretary of State to Paul Pate.
He says he also worked on defense policy in the U.S. Senate and helped develop future officers at the Naval Academy.

paragraphs.text: Peterman grew up in Bettendorf, Iowa, and graduated from the U.S. Naval Academy.
He served 10 years as a Navy helicopter pilot, and he says he led sailors overseas during more than a decade as a naval officer.
He later worked at the Naval Academy as an honor education officer, helping develop future officers.
He also spent a year as a legislative fellow for U.S. Sen. Jeanne Shaheen, and he says he worked on defense policy in the Senate.
Peterman announced in May 2025 that he would run for secretary of state.
He advanced from the June 2, 2026 Democratic primary and faced Republican incumbent Paul Pate in the November 3 general election.
He says he has met with county auditors in small towns and big cities across the state and wanted to be a partner they can trust.
During the campaign, he ran on making sure every eligible Iowan can vote and on rebuilding trust in elections.
He received 46.8% of the vote to Paul Pate's 53.2%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
